questions.question: Studies show that most riders in crashes:

options.text: Do not brake hard enough with the front tire and brake too hard with the rear tire.
Brake too hard with the front tire and do not brake hard enough with the rear tire.
Only use the front brake.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake hard enough with the front tire and brake too hard with the rear tire.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes do not brake hard enough with the front tire and brake too hard with the rear tire.

questions.question: The center portion of a lane:

options.text: Is always the best place for a motorcycle to ride.
Has oil and grease on it, but is usually safe to ride on.
Has oil and grease on it, and is never safe to ride on.
Is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has oil and grease on it, but is usually safe to ride on.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of each lane. On dry roads, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles to ride safely. You should still avoid areas with thick buildup of oil and grease, which are common at busy intersections and toll booths.

questions.question: When exiting a highway while riding in a group, use which formation?

options.text: Staggered
Single-file
Paired up
Three riders across the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Groups should ride in a staggered formation for most situations. However, switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting highways.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, you should:

options.text: Stay in the same lane position throughout the entire curve.
Stay in the left portion of the lane throughout the entire curve.
Stay in the right portion of the lane throughout the entire curve.
Remember that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remember that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change all the time. Be ready to change your lane position whenever needed. The best path through a curve may not match the shape of the road.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, you should:

options.text: Always ride in the center portion of the lane.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane.
Always ride in the right portion of the lane.
Be flexible and consider many factors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible and consider many factors.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. You do not need to avoid any portion of the lane at all times. Choose the position where you are most visible and can keep space around you.

questions.question: On wet roads, you should avoid:

options.text: The left portion of a lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.
All areas of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks builds up in a strip down the center of each lane. This strip normally has enough grip for safe riding, except when wet. The strip is usually narrow enough that you can ride beside it and stay in the center area of the lane.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Speed up.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Oil deposits in the center strip of a lane become dangerous when wet. When rain starts, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Also slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: Yellow signs with black lettering or symbols are what type of sign?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Lean their shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit as upright as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by releasing the throttle and using the brakes if needed.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have curved, or convex, mirrors. These mirrors:

options.text: Are easy to adjust to right away.
Make cars look closer than they really are.
Show a narrow view of the road.
Make cars look farther away than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give a wider view than flat mirrors. They also make objects look farther away than they actually are. Practice judging distances in convex mirrors if you are not used to them.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is never safe for motorcyclists.
Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided because other parts of the lane do not have oil.
Improves traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars drips and collects in a strip in the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area has enough grip for motorcyclists to ride safely. The strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can ride to one side of it and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When do you not need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When the road is slippery
When there is heavy traffic
When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
When it is raining

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle needs more distance to stop. You need more distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if heavy traffic means another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Do not swerve. Use only the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: The best way to brake in a straight line is by:

options.text: Using the rear brake only.
Using the front brake only.
Using both brakes.
Using the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes fully to stop in a straight line. Do not lock either wheel. Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If road conditions require a longer stopping distance, you should:

options.text: Decrease your following distance.
Increase your following distance.
Travel on the shoulder.
Let someone else operate your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle needs more distance to stop. This includes when the road is slippery, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when heavy traffic means another driver might cut in front of you. Keep a minimum three-second following distance.

questions.question: The right footwear for riding a motorcycle has:

options.text: Long, loose laces.
Short heels.
Tall heels.
Always sneakers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Short heels.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels may catch on rough surfaces. Tuck in laces so they cannot get caught on anything.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride more slowly than normal.
Start slowing earlier than normal.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: The passenger's weight makes your motorcycle respond more slowly. Ride slower than usual, slow down sooner, and increase your following distance. Always tell your passenger about road hazards ahead.

questions.question: The center of a lane usually has an oily strip. This part of the lane is:

options.text: Never safe for motorcyclists.
Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe, regardless of weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars drips and collects in a strip in the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area has enough grip for motorcyclists to ride safely. The strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can ride to one side of it and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should tell them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should avoid unnecessary conversation and movement so you can focus on riding. Passengers should board only after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which factor does not affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How fast the alcohol was consumed
How often a person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: how much alcohol was consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and food intake may also have some effect.
